$comment: How the gateway names the principals it acts for, under the knowledge base's domain (its committed `site.domain`). Every principal is named by the subject its issuer asserted, under the kind its token says it is: an agent's account carries the claim `kind` holding `agent`, and any other is a person's. A person is `did:web:{domain}:users:{subject}` and an agent `did:web:{domain}:agents:{subject}`, where the subject is the value of the claim `identity.subjectClaim` names. Every part of a DID after the domain is percent-encoded as ECMAScript's encodeURIComponent does: each UTF-8 byte of a character other than A–Z a–z 0–9 - _ . ! ~ * ' ( ) becomes %XX in uppercase hex; the domain is written as it is. An engine — a provider and a model, which is no principal — is given the name `{provider} {model}`, which a worker states as its own unless it says otherwise. Every implementation that names these principals runs every case and fails on a difference, and a running gateway is held to every case too.

absent.typescript: No TypeScript code names a principal: the gateway, in Rust, mints every DID it acts for.

notYetReached.kotlin: The Kotlin SDK's names of the principals the gateway acts for.
